run.why: EM-9 and EM-10 both require the same commit, host and window. Two separate runs would differ by exactly the run-to-run variance 4.4 records - 7.1x on this target - and the ratio between the regimes would be uninterpretable.

miss_body.statement: 60 KB of ordinary text carries no literal the Aho-Corasick prefilter can find, so the P1-7 skip FIRES and the full regex never runs. Asserted here, before any timing.

hit_body.statement: 40 KB of ordinary text containing a SQL-shaped substring. The prefilter ADMITS it, so the full regex RUNS. Asserted here, before any timing. The substring is benign and the endpoint is expected to serve the request - the property asserted is the PREFILTER'S, not a detection.

scan_cost.ceiling_basis: absolute, chosen BEFORE measurement, never relaxed
scan_cost.ratio_note: HIT/MISS at DIFFERENT body sizes. The hit body is SMALLER, so this ratio UNDERSTATES the per-byte penalty: the hit regime costs more while scanning 33% fewer bytes. Per-KB figures are reported beside it so the per-byte story is not hidden by the size difference.
scan_cost.per_kb_ratio_note: COST PER KILOBYTE, which removes the size confound entirely. This is the figure that describes the regime boundary; the raw ratio above is kept for completeness and is the more conservative one.
